findings.F1: The tested result is on the predicted side but held down by a few extreme cases. The 113 cases have a mean short-signed unusual move of +1.33 % over 5 days (t 1.09), while their median is +2.08 %, 64 % of them are positive, the 5 % trimmed mean is +1.74 % and the Wilcoxon p is 0.019; the single worst case is −84.5 % against a best of +51.8 %.
findings.F2: The effect appears only when the failed breakout comes inside a falling market.
findings.F3: The effect changes sign from year to year, so the market's own regime drowns it. 2022 gives +16.5 % (t 3.44, 9 cases) and 2025 +3.75 % (t 2.52, 20 cases), while 2020 gives −4.83 % (t −1.68, 9 cases) and 2024 −1.91 % (t −1.05, 24 cases).
findings.F4: The plan's 5-day horizon is not where the effect is clearest.
findings.F5: The depth of the close under the breakout low grades the move only weakly. The Spearman correlation is 0.199, and by depth tercile the means are −1.18 % (t −0.44), +3.61 % (t 1.85) and +1.62 % (t 1.10), so the move does not rise steadily with depth.
findings.F6: The effect sits mostly in the six long-history coins.
findings.F7: The test already used all 19 coins on all four folds of daily data, so more of the same data cannot lift the t. A clear answer needs the idea narrowed to where its move shows (F2).

ideas.idea: When a failed breakout above the prior 20-day high ends with a daily close below the low of the breakout day, the coin falls over the next 5 days, only while the coin's 60-day return is negative, and the further that close sits below the breakout day's low, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would short failed breakouts that are counter-trend rallies in a falling coin, and refuse to short them while the coin is in a rising 60-day trend.
ideas.name: failed breakout in downtrend
